variant_desc: high-register-pressure hot loop where if-vs-cmov lowering is fragile
source_citation: https://www.memorysafety.org/blog/rav1d-performance-optimization/ — rav1d Feb 2026: adding an unrelated TxClass variant changed stack usage and flipped LLVM from cmov to branch on this exact shape
novelty_rationale: Tests whether the LLM knows to write explicit bitmask formulation (mask = -(cond); out = (a & mask) | (b & ~mask)) when cmov-vs-branch lowering is fragile to surrounding register pressure. The compiler optimizes for register-pressure heuristics the programmer cannot influence at source level except by removing the if entirely. CALIBRATION CAVEAT: rav1d documented this on x86_64 Clang where adding a TxClass enum variant flipped lowering from cmov to branch. On Apple Silicon ARM with a 50/50 branch the predictor handles it fine and the gap closes to 1x; on x86 with deep speculation the gap is larger but still subtle. Pattern is real even when the test machine doesn't surface it.
